name: CSA2 Reuse · source layer 25 · csa2 bf16

sources.text: Four ordered decoder attention fragments corresponding to layers 20,21,24,25, omitting intervening layers and all non-attention network components. This is not the complete model or a benchmark prediction. One query per decode call. Artificial H=4, query/output ranks=2, one attention/index head, D=16, index D=8, window=2, Top-K=2, one candidate block of width 2. Existing cache is initialized and append/window updates reserve the call-end capacity in place. Profiles are counterfactual all-Full, main/indexer-K sharing with four index computations, and source-pattern Full/Reuse/Reindex/Reuse. Each counterfactual is explicit graph data, not an inferred reuse ratio. BF16 weights and matrix arithmetic, explicit FP32 vector proxies for normalization, rotary transform, packing, selection and unpacking. Cache payload/metadata accesses and independent staging buffers are declared separately. In the packed variant, indexer K unpack is an explicit vector segment inside the score leaf, using registers with no additional HBM backing. Gather and index-key unpack increase executed operations only; cache representation does not increase model-useful arithmetic. The packed theoretical variant uses row-local FP4 main/index and FP8 window payloads with one-byte scale metadata; the BF16 cache variant keeps uncompressed allocation. Neither claims bitwise numerical equivalence to the inference demo. Artificial 4096-byte device, matrix/vector 1000 operations/s and HBM 100 bytes/s. Ideal streams ignore contention; shared_bandwidth is the existing declared-HBM resource model. No kernel fusion, communication, allocator slack or omitted model components are inferred.
